name: Gilead
overview: Gilead was a male member of the tribe of Reuben, distinguished as a son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh. He is noted in Scripture as the progenitor of the Gileadites, a clan identified in Numbers 26:29. His lineage situates him within the broader family of the Israelite tribes, emphasizing his role in the genealogical records.
namesAndTitles: The name Gilead means 'perhaps monument of stones,' indicating a possible symbolic or geographical significance. This proper name is not recorded as being given directly by God but holds meaning that may reflect a memorial or landmark context within the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Gilead as the son of Machir, who is the grandson of Manasseh, confirming his place in the tribal genealogy. Additionally, inferred relationships include several descendants such as Iezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Shemida, and Hepher, as well as a brother named Hammolecheth, illustrating a well-documented family line within the tribe of Reuben.
scriptureSignificance: Gilead's significance lies primarily in his genealogical role as the ancestor of the Gileadites, a distinct clan within the tribe of Reuben. His lineage is carefully preserved in the book of Numbers, underscoring the importance of tribal heritage and God's providential care in preserving Israel's family lines. This genealogical record reflects God's faithfulness in establishing and sustaining His covenant people through successive generations.
